'''''Star Wars Battlefront II''''' is a [[Star Wars video games|video game]] created by [[Electronic Arts]] and developed by [[DICE]], [[Motive Studios]], and [[Criterion Games]]. It was released on November 17, [[2017]]. The game is a sequel to the [[2015]]'s ''[[Star Wars Battlefront]]'' and includes content from all three film trilogies, and has three times as much content as the original had at launch.

==Plot summary==
The storyline predominantly follows [[Iden Versio]], [[commander]] of the [[Galactic Empire|Imperial]] [[Imperial Special Forces|Special Forces]] unit [[Inferno Squad]]. Upon witnessing the [[Battle of Endor|destruction]] of the [[DS-2 Death Star II Mobile Battle Station|second Death Star]], Versio's troops look to her for direction. Versio tells her troops that they will avenge [[Darth Sidious|the Emperor]].<ref name="Game">''Star Wars Battlefront II''</ref>

The story spans thirty years, beginning in the waning months of the [[Galactic Civil War]] and concluding at the [[Battle of Starkiller Base|destruction]] of [[Starkiller Base]].<ref name="Game" />

There are segments in the campaign where other characters are playable as well, including [[Luke Skywalker]], [[Han Solo]], [[Ben Solo|Kylo Ren]], [[Landonis Balthazar Calrissian|Lando Calrissian]], and [[Prince]]ss [[Leia Skywalker Organa Solo|Leia Organa]].<ref name="Game" />

==Gameplay==
===Overview===
The game returns to the roots of the classic Battlefront games, using a class-based system for infantry troopers with each class having a shared progression system, but with equipment differing depending on faction.<ref name="Game" />

The trooper classes offered are Assault, Heavy, Officer and [[Specialist]].<ref name="Game" />

[[File:This_looks_pretty_BF_II.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Galactic Assault on Yavin IV]]
More vehicles are included for all factions, including [[Tauntaun]]s and the [[All Terrain Reconnaissance Transport|AT-RT]]. Space battles also return with new [[starship]]s. Vehicles are also to be a part of a new customization and progression system.<ref name="Game" />

Vehicles, heroes, and reinforcements can be purchased in matches by gaining Battle Points through play rather than picking up a token as it was with the [[Star Wars: Battlefront|previous game]].<ref name="Game" />

Playable hero and villain characters from the films have been expanded upon, with players able to customize skills to their liking. Creative Director Bernd Diemer stated that he wanted the heroes to have more depth rather than feeling like a momentary power up.<ref name="Game" />

The game also featured [[Wikipedia:Loot box|loot boxes]].<ref name="Game" /> Initially, these loot crates, which could be purchased with money, contained game altering abilities, but due to receiving heavy criticism, microtransactions were temporarily disabled at launch. On March 16, 2018, microtransactions were confirmed to be returning, albeit for cosmetic items only, which could be directly purchased while loot boxes would only contain in-game currency and other cosmetics, such as emotes. Progression is now entirely linear; playing as a particular class allows players to upgrade its abilities and unlock new ones.<ref name="Progression">{{EA|url=games/starwars/battlefront/star-wars-battlefront-2/news/progression-update|text=Revamped Progression is Coming Soon}}</ref>

===Game Modes===
*Campaign: The game includes a brand-new [[canon]] storyline which bridges the gap between [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|''Star Wars'': Episode VI ''Return of the Jedi'']] and ''[[Star Wars: Episode VII The Force Awakens]]'', mainly focusing on the aftermath of the Battle of Endor and follows the journey of Inferno Squad, an elite Imperial squad of special forces troopers.<ref name="Game" />
*Arcade: This game mode brings offline single-player (and two player co-op on consoles) gameplay with and versus AI-controlled players in different battle scenarios, as well as allowing players to create custom scenarios of their own.<ref name="Game" />
*Instant Action: This game mode is exactly like Capital Supremacy's ground phase, except with AI instead of players. Play on a number of [[Clone Wars]], Rebel-Empire and Resistance-First Order era maps, such as Theed, Kashyyyk, Death Star II, Hoth, Ajan Kloss, and Takodana as either of the several factions. Instant Action also has an additional mode (called Instant Action Missions) in which players either attack or defend various command posts to advance or stop the attack. This feature was released in the Battle on Scarif update and is similar to the online co-op mode.<ref name="Game" />
*Multiplayer: Multiplayer includes different online game modes which can support up to 40 players simultaneously.<ref name="Game" />
**Galactic Assault: 20v20 battles with unique objectives for thirteen maps, which include [[Naboo]], [[Geonosis]], [[Kamino]], [[Kashyyyk]], [[Tatooine]], [[Yavin 4]], [[Hoth]], [[Endor]], [[DS-2 Death Star II Mobile Battle Station|the Second Death Star]], [[Jakku]], [[Takodana]], [[Starkiller Base]], and [[Crait]]. Participants can play as both troopers and heroes, as well as selected vehicles and starships depending on the map.<ref name="Game" />
**Starfighter Assault: 12v12 space battles with an additional 20 AI-controlled ships per team with unique objectives for maps both in space and in the skies of planets. Some of the planets such as [[Ryloth]], [[D'Qar]] and [[Fondor]] are only available to play on in Starfighter Assault as there is no ground map for these planets.<ref name="Game" />
**Strike: 8v8 mode where two teams compete in small-scale objective based scenarios.<ref name="Game" />
**Blast: 8v8 team deathmatch.<ref name="Game" />
**Heroes vs. Villains: 4v4 hero duels involving characters from all three eras.<ref name="Game" />
**Ewok Hunt: A tag-like gamemode where stormtroopers (starting with 18 troopers) face off against Ewoks (starting with 2 Ewoks) in the dark.<ref name="Game" />
**Hero Showdown: 2v2 hero duels involving characters from all three eras.<ref name="Game" />
**Extraction: A gamemode involving teams of up to 8 where a Rebel team attempt to move a valuable shipment through imperial territory in close quarter combat.<ref name="Game" />
**Jetpack Cargo: A now inaccessible mode where two teams try to capture a shipment. The first to three captures wins.<ref name="Game" />
**Hero Starfighter: 4v4 space battles with hero starfighters.<ref name="Game" />
**Supremacy (also referred to as Capital Supremacy): A mode taking place in all 3 eras featuring five command posts that teams consisting of 20 players and AI fight for control over. In [[Prequel trilogy|Age of the Republic]] and [[Sequel trilogy|Age of Resistance]], the first team to reach 100% attacks the enemy team's capital ship, similar to conquest from [[Star Wars: Battlefront II|''Star Wars: Battlefront II'' (2005)]]. If the attackers fail, both teams return to the ground phase of combat and keep fighting until one capital ship is destroyed. In [[Original trilogy|Age of Rebellion]], the mode is similar, but there is no ship phase.<ref name="Game" />
**Co-Op Missions: A mode where a team of 4 players and AI choose to take on the attacking or defending role against a team of AI.<ref name="Game" />

==Development==
The game's development was revealed in an interview with an EA executive in [[2016]].<ref name="New Battlefront" /> More information, including its development by [[DICE]] and [[Motive Studios]], was revealed during EA's Livestream during E3 2016.

The game's development is a collaboration between DICE, who developed the multiplayer, Motive Studios, who developed the single-player mode, and Criterion Software, who developed the vehicle and flight controls. The game includes content from all three film trilogies.<ref name="Reveal Trailer">{{EASWYouTube|Kae-JjbLsgA|Star Wars Battlefront II: Full Length Reveal Trailer|sw_url=video/star-wars-battlefront-ii-full-length-reveal-trailer}}</ref> A goal of the game's story is to humanize the Empire in ways that haven't been seen before.<ref name="IGNBattlefront">{{WebCite|url=http://www.ign.com/articles/2017/04/15/battlefront-2-single-player-preview|text=Star Wars Battlefront 2 Single-Player Preview|author=Alanah Pearce|date=2017-04-15|work=[[Wikipedia:IGN|''IGN'']]|archivedate=20170416092138}}</ref>

On April 12, 2017 a teaser trailer was leaked giving confirmation that the game would include content from all three main ''Star Wars'' eras, a single-player campaign, and heroes such as [[Ben Solo|Kylo Ren]], [[Rey Skywalker|Rey]], [[Maul|Darth Maul]], and [[Yoda]].<ref name="TeaserLeak">{{WebCite|url=http://www.independent.co.uk/arts-entertainment/films/news/star-wars-battlefront-2-trailer-leak-orlando-celebration-a7679921.html|text=Star Wars Battlefront 2 trailer leaks ahead of Orlando Celebration|author=Jack Shepherd|date=2017-04-12|work=[[Wikipedia:The Independent|''The Independent'']]|archivedate=20180128142317}}</ref> EA premiered this trailer the following day during their panel at 2017's [[Celebration Orlando]].<ref>{{EA|subdomain=starwars|url=starwars/battlefront/news/star-wars-battlefront-ii-celebration|text=Your First Look at STAR WARS Battlefront II Is Coming at STAR WARS Celebration}}</ref> A gameplay trailer for the game was released on June 10, 2017 during the Battlefront II panel at E3 2017.<ref name="EAPlayLive">{{OfficialYouTube|channel=@IGN|name=IGN|link=Wikipedia:IGN|video=R4Bta5UNTHw|text=E3 2017: EA Press Conference and EA Play - IGN LIVE}}</ref>

The single-player trailer was released in October 2017, with a preview on [[The Star Wars Show]].<ref name="Star Wars Show 10/18">{{StarWarsShow|4tLBy9FGS5A|New Battlefront II Trailer First Look, Author Chuck Wendig, and Solo Revealed!|sw_url=video/new-battlefront-ii-trailer-first-look-chuck-wendig-interview-and-the-han-solo-movie-title-revealed}}</ref>

While working on the game, the development team notably consulted [[Emil Fortune]]'s reference book ''[[Star Wars: Galactic Atlas]]''.<ref name="BTS">{{EASWYouTube|pryBP4K-_34|Star Wars Battlefront II: Behind The Story}}</ref> Additionally, the team worked with [[Lucasfilm]]'s [[Lucasfilm Story Group|Story Group]] on the campaign and characters, including making sure Luke Skywalker's character arc was consistent, and keeping the game in line with other ''Star Wars'' visuals, according to Game Director Mark Thompson.<ref name="OXM magazine">''Official Xbox Magazine'' summer 2017</ref>

[[Gordy Haab]] composed and orchestrated the [[Star Wars: Battlefront II (Original Video Game Soundtrack)|musical score]] of ''Star Wars Battlefront II''. The score was performed by the [[London Symphony Orchestra]] and [[London Voices]] at [[Abbey Road Studios]], and was nominated in the 2017 [[Wikipedia:Game Audio Network Guild Awards|Game Audio Network Guild Awards]].<ref name="Iden Versio Hero's Journey" />

===Downloadable content===
DICE hinted that the game would not include a season pass, unlike the previous game.<ref name="Mashable">{{WebCite|url=https://mashable.com/2017/04/15/star-wars-battlefront-2-season-pass-no-more|text=It looks like 'Star Wars: Battlefront II' will ditch the Season Pass|author=Adam Rosenberg|date=2017-04-15|work=[[Wikipedia:Mashable|Mashable]]|archivedate=20191201143619}}</ref> Instead, they wanted to find a better alternative in order to avoid "fragmenting" the community of players.<ref name="NME">{{WebCite|url=http://www.nme.com/news/star-wars-battlefront-will-not-season-pass-2054166|text='Star Wars: Battlefront II' will have 'something different' from a season pass|author=Nick Levine|date=2017-04-18|work=[[Wikipedia:NME|''NME'']]|archivedate=20170424231852}}</ref>
It was confirmed during EA Play 2017 that there would not be a season pass; rather, all downloadable content would be free for all players and included in events called Seasons.<ref name="EAPlayLive" />

====''The Last Jedi'' Season====
The first Season expansion, ''The Last Jedi'' Season was released on [[December 5]] and is centered around [[Star Wars: Episode VIII The Last Jedi|''Star Wars'': Episode VIII ''The Last Jedi'']], the eighth film in the ''[[Star Wars]]'' saga which was released on [[December 15]], [[2017]]. It features a space map over D'Qar, the new planet [[Crait]], [[Resistance]] hero [[Finn]] and First Order villain Captain [[Phasma]].<ref name="The Last Jedi expansion">{{EA|url=games/starwars/battlefront/star-wars-battlefront-2/news/the-last-jedi-season-is-coming|text=Choose a Side: The Last Jedi Season Is Coming}}</ref>

''The Last Jedi'' Season also featured a campaign addition available [[December 13]], named ''Battlefront II: Resurrection'', which details Commander Iden Versio's journey during the First Order's rise to power and contains three chapters.<ref name="The Last Jedi expansion" />

====''Solo'' Season====
On [[May 3]], EA Star Wars announced on Twitter that the second Season in the game would be based on the character of Han Solo, releasing alongside ''[[Solo: A Star Wars Story]]''.<ref name="Solo season">{{Twitter|EAStarWars|status/992088715836076033|[[Electronic Arts]]|quote=We've got a really good feeling about this. #StarWarsBattlefrontII: The Han Solo Season arrives this month. Details come out of hyperspace next week.}}</ref> The first part of the Han Solo Season was released on [[May 16]] and features the returning map set in [[Boba Fett's Palace|Jabba's Palace]], a new game mode (Hero Showdown), new skins for Leia Organa and Lando Calrissian based on their disguises in [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|''Star Wars'': Episode VI ''Return of the Jedi'']], and the addition of starfighters to Arcade. The second part of the Han Solo Season was revealed in a trailer on [[June 6]] and its content released on [[June 12]], which included a new map on [[Kessel]], the ''Millennium Falcon'' as it appears in ''Solo: A Star Wars Story'', the returning game mode Extraction, and new skins for Han Solo, Lando Calrissian, and Chewbacca as they appear in ''Solo: A Star Wars Story''.<ref name="Solo Season Reveal Trailer">{{EASWYouTube|UqCg5JcMvfk|Star Wars Battlefront II: The Han Solo Season}}</ref>

====''Clone Wars'' content====
The game's Design Director, [[Dennis Brännvall]], teased that ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]'' content was going to be added to the game at some point in the future.<ref name="Clone Wars content">{{WebCite|url=https://www.bleedingcool.com/2018/02/07/clone-wars-content-coming-star-wars-battlefront-ii|text=Clone Wars Content Is Coming To Star Wars Battlefront II|author=Patrick Dane|date=2018-02-07|archivedate=20200514134954}}</ref> At EA Play it was revealed that in the fall of 2018, a third season focused on the Clone Wars was going to be released, the season would include a map featuring [[Geonosis]], new Clone Trooper skins, and [[General]] [[Grievous]], [[Obi-Wan Kenobi]], Count [[Dooku]], and [[Anakin Skywalker]] as playable characters. General Grievous was released on October 30, 2018 with an alternate "Battle Damaged" appearance. Obi-Wan Kenobi together with the 212th Battalion skins and a "Shattered" General Grievous skin followed up on November 28 alongside the Geonosis Galactic Assault map. In December, a new appearance of Obi-Wan Kenobi titled "General Kenobi" was released, based on his ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]'' armor (prior to the mid-third season).

[[File:Dooku-BFII.jpg|thumb|left|300px|Count Dooku in ''Battlefront II'']]
Count Dooku was released on January 23, 2019, followed by an alternate "Dark Ritual" appearance less than a week later. Anakin Skywalker, along with the 501st and Coruscant Guard skins, and a general update for all Clone trooper skins, including armored clone officers, were released on February 27, 2019.

Also initially scheduled for February but then pushed back to March 26, 2019 was Capital Supremacy: a new, large-scale game mode, featuring both capture points and capital ship takedowns, as well as two new Clone Wars Era Reinforcements and lightsaber combat improvements, which included no more stagger to a hero whose attack is blocked, plus the requirement of stamina to attack. It also featured a new appearance for Count Dooku: His sleepwear. On March 12, 2019, two new reinforcement classes were announced: Dual DC-17 pistol-wielding [[Advanced Recon Commando|ARC Troopers]] and [[BX-series droid commando]]s, also released on March 26.<ref name="Reinforcements">{{EA|subdomain=battlefront-forums|url=discussion/132048/community-transmission-infiltrator-reinforcements|text=Community Transmission – Infiltrator Reinforcements}}</ref>

On April 2, 2019, three new locations were announced as being in development for Capital Supremacy. The first location, Kashyyyk, was released on April 24, and May and June release date for the next two. On May 10, 2019, the second location was revealed to be Kamino, and released on May 22. The third, Naboo, was revealed on June 7, 2019 - the first day of E3 2019 - and slated for a June 26 release,<ref name="June Calendar">{{EA|subdomain=battlefront-forums|url=discussion/138817/community-calendar-june|text=Community Calendar - June}}</ref> along with the unveiling of a large amount of upcoming content for the next few months. Among them were droidekas, Anakin Skywalker's Jedi General appearance from the early seasons of ''The Clone Wars'', the [[TX-130 Saber-class fighter tank|TX-130 ''Saber''-class fighter tank]], additional clone trooper skins, and another Capital Supremacy location, released on September 25, 2019: [[Felucia]].<ref name="Droidekas">{{EA|subdomain=battlefront-forums|url=discussion/137644/community-transmission-where-are-those-droidekas|text=Community Transmission – Where Are Those Droidekas}}</ref> A new type of enforcer was also released that same day: the [[Clone commando]].

====''The Rise of Skywalker'' content====
On December 4th 2019, DICE detailed the content coming December 17th, to tie into the release of ''The Rise of Skywalker. ''These included new appearances for Finn, Rey, and Kylo Ren, and a new planet, being the jungle world of [[Ajan Kloss]] based on the new movie. Four reinforcements were also added, the [[Sith trooper]] and a revamped Jet Trooper for the First Order, and two new ones for the Resistance, an [[Ovissian]] Gunner and a [[Caphex]] Spy. In January 2020, more content was released, with capital supremacy including the sequel era, as well as two new playable heroes, [[BB-8]] and [[BB-9E]].<ref name="EpisodeIXUpdate">{{EA|subdomain=battlefront-forums|url=discussion/149813/community-transmission-celebration-edition-the-rise-of-skywalker|text=Community Transmission – Celebration Edition & The Rise of Skywalker}}</ref>

====Original trilogy content====
Following the release of content from ''The Rise of Skywalker'', a new focus on content from the original trilogy was announced. The first update including this content was released in February 2020, which included a new appearance for Imperial Jet Troopers, as well as playable [[Ewok]] and [[Imperial Security Bureau]] [[agent]] reinforcements. New weapons were also added. Additionally, further content set for release in March 2020 was announced, which included the addition of the original trilogy content to other modes such as Supremacy, as well as the addition of Scarif. Capital Supremacy has been renamed "Supremacy" due to the lack of capital ships in the original trilogy settings of the game mode.<ref name="Age of Rebellion">{{EA|subdomain=battlefront-forums|url=discussion/155395/star-wars-battlefront-ii-the-age-of-rebellion-update|text=Star Wars Battlefront II - Age of Rebellion Update}}</ref>

==Release and reception==
In April 2017 during the presentation at Star Wars Celebration, it was confirmed that the game would be released on November 17, 2017 and November 14 for those pre ordering the Deluxe Elite Trooper Edition.<ref name="New Battlefront" /> An open beta was held from October 4 to October 11.<ref name="Pre Beta Details">{{EA|url=games/starwars/battlefront/star-wars-battlefront-2/news/pre-beta-details|text=Get Ready for the STAR WARS Battlefront II Beta}}</ref>

====Pre-release====
The game, alongside EA itself, was lambasted for locking Heroes and making players "grind" large amounts, some estimated to be around 40 hours, to unlock a single character, which in turn would encourage the purchases of Loot crates to make it easier for the player to unlock them. When EA responded to the criticism on Reddit, their comment received several hundred thousand downvotes, more than any other Reddit comment by magnitudes.<ref>{{WebCite|url=https://www.cnbc.com/2017/11/14/ea-star-wars-title-reducing-in-game-costs-after-pre-launch-backlash.html|text=EA is reducing in-game costs on its new 'Star Wars' title after pre-launch backlash|author=Sara Salinas|date=2017-11-14|work=[[Wikipedia:CNBC|CNBC]]|archivedate=20200413162443}}</ref> After the huge backlash and reception of the loot crate system, EA and DICE temporarily removed microtransactions from the game on launch to focus on refining the loot crate system for another time.<ref name="Gamespot">{{WebCite|url=https://www.gamespot.com/articles/shortly-before-star-wars-battlefront-2s-release-ea/1100-6455042|text=Shortly Before Star Wars: Battlefront 2's Release, EA Removes Microtransactions For Now|author=Eddie Makuch|date=2017-11-20|archivedate=20191203110812}}</ref>

====Post-release====
The game faced heavy criticism for its economic and progression system due to being tied to microtransactions that allowed players to purchase a certain amount of "crystals," an in-game currency, in order to then purchase loot crates that could be used to randomly unlock and upgrade Star Cards. Furthermore, the game received criticism for the high amount of "credits," another in-game currency, it cost in order to purchase playable hero and villain characters, which would take hundreds of hours of grinding in order to obtain. The fallout from the microtransactions scandal was massive enough to attract attention from mainstream news outlets such as [[Wikipedia:CNN|CNN]] and [[Wikipedia:The Wall Street Journal|''The Wall Street Journal'']].<ref>{{WebCite|url=https://money.cnn.com/2017/11/16/technology/battlefront-ii-star-wars-game-ea-costs/index.html|text=Star Wars video game maker apologizes after uproar from fans|author=Jethro Mullen and Ivana Kottasová|date=2017-11-17|work=[[Wikipedia:CNN|CNN]]|archivedate=20200428220607}}</ref><ref>{{WebCite|url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/electronic-arts-pulls-microtransactions-from-star-wars-battlefront-ii-after-fan-backlash-1510936871|text=Electronic Arts Pulls Microtransactions From Star Wars Battlefront II After Fan Backlash|author=Sarah Needleman and Ben Fritz|date=2017-11-17|work=[[Wikipedia:The Wall Street Journal|''The Wall Street Journal'']]|archivedate=20200505015919}}</ref> Disney and Lucasfilm have also publicly sided with gamers and criticized EA over the latter's handling of the game.<ref>{{WebCite|url=http://www.rollingstone.com/glixel/features/disney-sides-with-fans-in-battlefront-ii-cash-grab-w512229|text=Disney/Lucasfilm Side With Fans in Star Wars Battlefront II Cash Grab|author=Brian Crecente|date=2017-11-20|work=[[Wikipedia:Rolling Stone|''Rolling Stone'']]|archivedate=20171121095434}}</ref><ref>{{WebCite|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/news/comic-riffs/wp/2017/11/18/how-a-star-wars-video-game-faced-charges-that-it-was-promoting-gambling|text=How a Star Wars video game faced charges that it was promoting gambling|author=Gene Park|date=2017-11-18|work=[[Wikipedia:The Washington Post|''The Washington Post'']]|archivedate=20200225042230}}</ref> Along with reportedly having the potential to harm the game's sales prospects, the incident also further hurt EA's public image; EA's shares on Wall Street dropped by 2.5% on launch day.<ref>{{WebCite|url=https://www.cnbc.com/2017/11/17/wall-street-is-freaking-out-as-ea-caves-again-to-social-media-outrage-over-its-star-wars-game.html|text=Wall Street is freaking out as EA caves again to social media outrage over its Star Wars game|author=Tae Kim|date=2017-11-17|work=[[Wikipedia:CNBC|CNBC]]|archivedate=20200429194527}}</ref>

In response to the criticism, microtransactions were immediately disabled at launch, albeit temporarily. The cost to purchase heroes was also lowered by 75%. On March 16, 2018, developer DICE announced microtransactions would be returning in April, which can only be used to purchase cosmetic items; the progression system was redesigned in order to be linear, and was released on March 21.<ref name="Progression" />

Since then, the game continues to have an active playerbase and has had more positive reception, primarily due to its reworking of its progression systems and the removal of its microtransactions in the Celebration Edition. The game notably had a resurgence in player count in May 2025 fueled by its inclusion into [[Wikipedia:Xbox Game Pass|Xbox Game Pass]],<ref name="Game Pass">{{WebCite|url=https://www.gamespot.com/articles/star-wars-battlefront-2s-best-version-is-free-for-game-pass-members-right-now/1100-6528572|text=Star Wars: Battlefront 2's Best Version Is Free For Game Pass Members Right Now|author=Eddie Makuch|date=2014-12-19|archivedate=20250601125248}}</ref> the final season of ''[[Star Wars: Andor]]'',<ref name="Slashfilm">{{WebCite|url=https://www.slashfilm.com/1871771/star-wars-battlefront-2-video-game-comeback-players-surge|text=A Star Wars Video Game Is Having An Unexpected Comeback Years After Its Original Release|author=Ryan Scott|date=2025-05-28|work=[[Wikipedia:/Film|''/Film'']]|archivedate=20250603163806}}</ref> the twentieth-anniversary re-release of ''[[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith|Revenge of the Sith]]'' in theaters, and a new ''Star Wars''-themed ''[[Fortnite]]'' season.<ref name="Game Rant">{{WebCite|url=https://gamerant.com/star-wars-battlefront-2-player-surge-2025-andor-fortnite-explained-why|text=Why Players Are Flocking Back to Star Wars Battlefront 2 in 2025|author=LB Beistad|date=2025-05-23|work=[https://gamerant.com Game Rant]|archivedate=20250604112536}}</ref> On May 24, 2025, the game's concurrent player count on Steam surged to almost 19,000 concurrent players, breaking the previous all-time peak of 10,000 concurrent players. Fan demand for a third ''Battlefront'' game rose significantly, with many ex-developers and actors who worked on the wider ''Star Wars'' franchise taking notice and joining them,<ref name="GamesRadar">{{WebCite|url=https://www.gamesradar.com/games/fps/former-star-wars-battlefront-2-dev-says-we-want-to-get-the-gang-back-together-for-a-potential-sequel-as-the-game-surges-in-popularity-once-more|text=Former Star Wars Battlefront 2 dev says "we want to get the gang back together" for a potential sequel as the game surges in popularity once more|author=Scott McCrae|date=2025-05-23|work=[[Wikipedia:GamesRadar+|''GamesRadar+'']]|archivedate=20250724180542}}</ref> among them actor [[Muhannad Bhaier]], who portrayed [[Wilmon Paak]] in ''Andor''.<ref name="ComicBook.com">{{WebCite|url=https://comicbook.com/gaming/news/star-wars-battlefront-3-support-andor-actor-muhannad-ben-amor|text=Star Wars Battlefront 3 Campaign Gets Support from Andor Actor|author=Cade Onder|date=2025-05-21|work=[[Wikipedia:ComicBook.com|''ComicBook.com'']]|archivedate=20250623192435}}</ref> This was further fueled by an EA-held sale event on Steam in June 2025 that further pushed the player count to nearly 36,000 concurrent players, breaking the previous record set in May.<ref name="TweakTown">{{WebCite|url=https://www.tweaktown.com/news/105954/battlefront-ii-player-count-surges-by-1100-on-steam-will-ea-take-notice/index.html|text=Battlefront II player count surges by 1100% on Steam, will EA take notice?|author=Derek Strickland|date=2025-06-22|work=[https://www.tweaktown.com TweakTown]|archiveurl=https://archive.ph/BpVgn}}</ref>

===Controversies===
EA's incorporation of loot boxes into the ''Battlefront II'' game has also attracted the attention of several governments. On November 15, the Belgian Gaming Commission announced that it would be investigating whether the inclusion of loot boxes constituted gambling. In response, EA denied allegations that their loot boxes constituted gambling, asserting they were part of a "fun and fair game experience."<ref>{{WebCite|url=https://www.pcgamesn.com/star-wars-battlefront-2/battlefront-2-loot-box-gambling-belgium-gaming-commission|text=Sadly, the Belgium Government has not yet declared loot boxes gambling|author=Dustin Bailey|date=2017-11-22|work=[[Wikipedia:PCGamesN|''PCGamesN'']]|archivedate=20200413163722}}</ref> On November 22, the Belgian Gambling Commission ruled that EA's microtransactions constituted a form of gambling. The [[Wikipedia:Minister of Justice (Belgium)|Belgian Minister of Justice]] [[Wikipedia:Koen Geens|Koen Geens]] also regarded the "mixing of gaming and gambling as dangerous" for the mental health of children and called for a ban on gaming loot boxes throughout the European Union.<ref>{{WebCite|url=https://www.gizmodo.com.au/2017/11/belgian-gaming-commission-decides-battlefront-2-style-loot-boxes-are-gambling-wants-them-banned|text=Belgian Gaming Commission Decides Battlefront 2-Style Loot Boxes Are Gambling, Wants Them Banned|author=Tom McKay|date=2017-11-22|work=[[Wikipedia:Gizmodo|''Gizmodo'']]|archivedate=20171122044215}}</ref><ref>{{WebCite|url=https://www.pcgamer.com/belgium-says-loot-boxes-are-gambling-wants-them-banned-in-europe|text=Belgium's Justice Minister calls for loot box ban in Europe (Updated)|author=Andy Chalk|date=2017-11-23|work=[[Wikipedia:PC Gamer|''PC Gamer'']]|archivedate=20200429195846}}</ref>

In response to the Belgian Gambling Commission's investigation, the Dutch Gambling Commission also announced their own investigation into microtransactions in ''Battlefront II''.<ref name="BNNVARA">{{WebCite|url=https://www.bnnvara.nl/kassa/videos/296128|text=Zorgen online games voor een gokverslaving bij kinderen?|date=2017-11-18|work=[[Wikipedia:BNNVARA|BNNVARA]]|language=Dutch|archivedate=20200514133618}}</ref> EA's practices also drew criticism from United States politicians.<ref name="Variety">{{WebCite|url=https://variety.com/2017/digital/news/star-wars-video-game-controversy-microtransaction-loot-box-1202621913|text=Star Wars Video Game Microtransactions Ignite Controversy|author=Matt Fernandez|date=2017-11-23|work=[[Wikipedia:Variety (magazine)|''Variety'']]|archivedate=20190828233233}}</ref><ref name="Kotaku">{{WebCite|url=https://www.kotaku.com.au/2017/11/hawaii-wants-to-fight-the-predatory-behavior-of-loot-boxes|text=Hawaii Wants To Fight The Predatory Behaviour Of Loot Boxes|author=Luke Plunkett|date=2017-11-22|work=[[Wikipedia:Kotaku|''Kotaku'']]|archivedate=20200308051002}}</ref>

In addition, gambling regulators in South Korea, Singapore, Australia, and the United Kingdom have also expressed disapproval of Electronic Arts' incorporation of loot boxes into gaming products including ''Battlefront II''.<ref name="Straits Times">{{WebCite|url=https://www.straitstimes.com/singapore/cool-loot-or-gambling-trap|text=Loot boxes in video games: Cool rewards or gambling trap?|author=Lester Hio|date=2017-12-10|work=[[Wikipedia:The Straits Times|''The Straits Times'']]|archivedate=20180921191028}}</ref><ref name="Economist">{{WebCite|url=https://www.economist.com/news/business/21732157-what-comes-out-loot-box-lot-lottery-video-games-could-fall-foul|text=Video games could fall foul of anti-gambling laws|date=2017-12-07|work=[[Wikipedia:The Economist|''The Economist'']]|archivedate=20180921225904}}</ref>

==Continuity==
*During the game's first mission, [[Admiral]] [[Gial Ackbar]] can be seen explaining [[Operation Yellow Moon]] from the book ''[[Moving Target: A Princess Leia Adventure]]'' to the crew of the ''[[Invincible Faith]]'' via a [[hologram]] transmission. Rebel soldiers can also be heard discussing the upcoming Battle of Endor and mentioning [[Gold Squadron (Rebel Alliance)|Gold Squadron]], [[Green Squadron (Rebel Alliance)|Green Squadron]], [[Blade Squadron]], a B-wing starfighter squadron that served as the focus of the [[Blade Squadron (short story)|''Blade Squadron'']] short story series, [[Corona Squadron]], which appears in the book ''Lost Stars'', and [[Red Squadron (Rebel Alliance)|Red Squadron]].
*During the Battle of Endor level, [[Garrick Versio]] mentions that [[Vice Admiral]] [[Rae Sloane]] ordered all Imperial ships to retreat. The order first appeared in the short story "[[The Levers of Power]]."
*[[Operation: Cinder]] first appeared in the [[Shattered Empire 2|second]] issue of the comic series ''[[Star Wars: Shattered Empire]]''.
*The compass that Luke Skywalker recovers from Emperor Palpatine's vault in the mission "The Observatory" can be seen in Luke's hut on [[Ahch-To]] in [[Star Wars: Episode VIII The Last Jedi|''Star Wars: The Last Jedi'']].
*During the Mission to [[Bespin]], several references to [[Governor]] [[Ubrik Adelhard]] and the [[Uprising]] can be heard. The Uprising first appeared in the mobile video game ''[[Star Wars: Uprising]]''.
*During the [[Battle of Jakku]] level, X-wing pilot chatter can be heard. Among those voices, references to [[Wedge Antilles]], [[Temmin Wexley|Snap Wexley]], and [[Phantom Squadron]] can be heard. Also, [[Thane Kyrell]], [[Kendy Idele]], and the ''[[Inflictor]]'' can be heard. Kyrell and Idele first appeared in the novel ''[[Lost Stars]]''.
*Garrick Versio mentions that [[Gallius Rax]] expected Versio to flee; this was part of the [[Contingency]]. Both Gallius and the Contigency appeared first in the [[Star Wars: The Aftermath Trilogy|''Aftermath'' trilogy]].
*[[Han Solo]] has a beard during the [[Takodana]] level, gathering intelligence for an upcoming raid on [[Kashyyyk]]. Solo was depicted as growing a scruffy beard during the ''Aftermath'' trilogy.
*Three of the game's achievements are called "Dark Forces", "Force Unleashed", and "Outbound Flight", probably referencing the now-[[Star Wars Legends|Legends]] video games and novel ''[[Star Wars: Dark Forces]]'', ''[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed]]'', and [[Outbound Flight (novel)|''Outbound Flight'']].
